# S55 — TUI color and visual polish: status, priority, focus, and feedback

**Findings:** user request: clearer TUI with color · **Size: M** · **Tree:** slicer

## Why

The user requested color and better TUI UI/UX. The current drawing loop in
src/slicer/tui.py uses normal, reverse, bold, and dim attributes, without a color
palette. Row already exposes status and blocked state; panel exposes field/section
entries. Use those structures to make status, priority, pane focus, and feedback
easier to scan while preserving readable text.

Related items: S41 covers search/filter/jump/help; S42 covers faster reordering;
S50 covers a creation wizard. This slice is presentation work and can ship independently.

## Files

- src/slicer/tui.py: semantic presentation roles, palette setup, row/detail drawing,
  pane focus, and typed feedback.
- tests/test_cli.py: existing TUI behavior/rows/panel tests; add focused presentation
  tests in a new tests/test_tui_style.py.
- docs/getting-started.md and README.md: describe visual cues and monochrome behavior.

## Failing tests

1. Pure role selection maps configured status roles, including custom vocabulary,
   to styles; unknown/custom extra statuses remain neutral.
2. Active blocked items keep a visible ! marker. Priority retains numeric/text cues.
3. Focused selection remains obvious over every status color; inactive selection
   remains visible without looking focused.
4. Monochrome and color initialization failures retain usable selection and labels.
5. Success, error, and informational outcomes carry explicit severity, including
   editor errors and validation failures; styling never guesses from message text.
6. Fake-screen drawing covers clipping, resize, and small terminal dimensions without
   out-of-bounds writes; existing movement/editing/action behavior remains covered.

## Implement

Keep stdlib curses and the existing pure-function presentation architecture. Add
semantic roles (normal, heading, started, done, parked, blocked, priority, success,
error, info) and resolve them to curses attributes only in the terminal layer.
Avoid putting escape sequences into Row.text or PanelLine.text.

Use a small basic-color palette on the terminal's default background: cyan for
started/headings, green for done/success, yellow for parked/blocked and high priority,
red for errors, neutral for open/other statuses and body text. Resolve named status
roles through Config fields rather than hardcoded status strings. Keep labels,
numeric scores, and blocked markers so no meaning relies solely on hue.
Show a compact labeled base priority score in the queue and retain the score/quadrant
detail. Emphasize priority 3 on either axis without changing ranking or queue order.

Initialize color once inside the curses session, checking capability and available
pairs. Prefer the terminal's default background. Fall back to monochrome if color,
default-background support, or palette initialization is unavailable. Respect a
nonempty NO_COLOR environment variable. No theme dependency or config migration.

Give panes explicit headings and a visible focus indicator. Focused selection uses
reverse plus bold and takes precedence over row colors; inactive selection uses
bold with a textual selection marker. Detail headings and editable fields have
consistent visual hierarchy. Preserve existing key bindings and pane navigation.

Add an explicit message severity to action/edit outcomes. Preserve apply_edit's
existing string-return interface through a wrapper if needed by current callers;
the run loop should consume the typed result. Informational no-ops and cancellations
must not be painted as successful mutations. Use visible Error:/OK:/Info: prefixes
alongside styling. Keep the normal help line neutral.

Reserve layout space for headings and feedback, clamp dimensions after resize, and
show a short resize prompt when the panes cannot fit. Centralize bounded drawing
rather than masking arbitrary curses failures throughout the UI. Preserve editor
suspend/resume and redraw behavior.

**Not in this slice:** search/filter/help overlay (S41), reorder shortcuts (S42),
wizard (S50), mouse controls, user-editable themes, a new TUI framework, CLI colors,
or changes to roadmap state/priority semantics.

## Check

Run focused presentation tests and existing TUI behavior tests, then the regression
suite. Run slicer check after updating roadmap state.

Manually inspect the TUI on light and dark terminal backgrounds and with NO_COLOR:
open/started/done/parked/custom statuses, active blocked items, priority emphasis,
both pane selections, prose, successful actions, invalid edits, editor cancellation,
long titles, narrow windows, and resizing. Record which terminal checks were actually
performed and any unavailable environment. Colors should aid scanning while every
state remains understandable without them.

## Git

Implement as a reviewable slice with code, tests, documentation, and generated roadmap
